title: Provision one throwaway AWS account end to end by hand, and time it
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing
- **Runs in parallel with:** the template task
- **Unblocks:** the setup fee, the queue rate, and the promise on the pitch page

---
A task, not a story, because the deliverable is a measured number and a written runbook rather than a behavior the system exhibits.

Stand up a fresh AWS account, run the cross-account setup as a customer would experience it, provision one organization computer, and run one bot task. Record what actually happened: elapsed wall-clock time, how much of it was waiting on AWS, which steps needed a human decision, and every place the instructions were wrong.

**Nothing else in this initiative can be honestly scheduled or priced until this number exists.** The setup fee prices this session. The invitation rate is capped by how many of these can be run per week. The pitch page makes a promise about how long onboarding takes. All three are currently guesses.

**Done when:** a runbook exists in the wiki, with a measured elapsed time and a list of the steps that needed a person.

comments.text:
# ▶ NEXT ACTION (2026-09-07)

**This is the next thing to work on.** Storage discovery is closed (`chatticus-e9ddec`, epic closed today) and nothing on the P0 list is blocked by it. This task is P0, blocked by nothing, and its one known obstacle is resolved.

## Why this one

- The parent epic says it outright: *"Start with: provisioning one throwaway account end to end by hand. Nothing else in this initiative can be scheduled or priced until that elapsed time is known."*
- `chatticus-8a25af` (P0, in_progress) **cannot close without it** — its done-condition is *"the hand-provisioning task ran against them unmodified."* The template is published; this run is what validates it.
- Three numbers currently guessed depend on the result: the **$100 setup fee** (`54f1cf`, `b4f849`), the **invitation rate** (how many of these can be run per week), and the **onboarding promise on the pitch page**. Prices are already chosen — this run tells you whether they are defensible.

## The blocker is cleared

The CloudFormation obstacle is resolved and the runbook landed in `infra/README.md` via #309:

- GET `https://dev.chattic.us/provisioning/customer-role.yml`
- then `aws cloudformation create-stack --template-body`
- **do not** pass the CloudFront URL as `--template-url` — CloudFormation rejects it

## Run it as a customer would

Fresh AWS account, cross-account setup exactly as a customer experiences it, provision one organization computer, run one bot task. Use the published template **unmodified** — if you have to edit it, that is a finding about `8a25af`, not a workaround.

## Record, per the description

Elapsed wall-clock; how much was waiting on AWS; which steps needed a human decision; **every place the instructions were wrong**. The last one is the most valuable output and the easiest to skip while working.

**Done when:** a runbook exists in the wiki with a measured elapsed time and the list of steps that needed a person.

comments.text:
**Method note:** AWS Organizations is **not** in use on `335163751677` and will **not** be enabled for this run. `CreateAccount` is off the table.

The remaining path is a **consumer** AWS account (aws.amazon.com signup: email, phone, payment) plus a CLI session in that account. Anthus root cannot stand in as the customer home — that only proves same-account start.

T0 remains blocked until that second account exists. If this desk cannot create one, that fact itself belongs in the wiki (invitation-rate / setup-fee input): we cannot complete a customer-shaped provision from a single billed account.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Do not stand up AWS Organizations for this run.** A customer does not join an Anthus org and does not get `CreateAccount`. `customer-role.yml` trusts Anthus `335163751677` from a **separate** billed account via AssumeRole + ExternalId.

What to do instead: one normal aws.amazon.com signup (email, phone, payment). Use **that** account as the throwaway customer. Time the signup — that wall-clock is the onboarding number. Then GET the published template in that account and `--template-body`.

A new management account plus Organization would measure Anthus-internal account vending, not self-setup, and would still require a first consumer signup anyway. Do not enable Organizations on `335163751677`.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Lab bookkeeping is a wiki row (account id, purpose, destroy-after), not AWS Organizations. Inviting the throwaway into an Anthus org would make it Anthus-controlled (consolidated billing, SCPs, management-account reach) and is not what a customer account looks like. Do not enable Organizations on `335163751677` as a side effect of this timing run.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Method amendment (one-person desk):** consolidated billing for *Anthus lab throwaways* is accepted. That is not the customer funnel.

- Enable Organizations on existing `335163751677` (do not invent a second management account; do not move Chatticus stacks).
- `CreateAccount` a member named as the b88c0a throwaway. One bill. Distinct account id, so AssumeRole + published template still apply.
- **Do not claim we timed aws.amazon.com signup.** Wiki must say: consumer phone/card funnel skipped; measured time is Chatticus provision (template, role, org record, computer, bot) plus Organizations `CreateAccount` wait.
- No SCPs that pretend this is a locked-down customer. Real customers stay *out* of this org.

Pitch/$100/invitation-rate: use the Chatticus-provision number; treat AWS account signup as unmeasured (or a separate stopwatch if someone later does a true consumer signup).
